verdicts.note: Self-references as 'a girl' doing civil engineering; whole interview is a woman engineer.
Quote says 'private high school' in Canada; she deflects the all-girls question and never confirms single-sex. Does not support code 2.
'I decided to do civil' confirms Civil & Building Engineering.
'satisfying things in engineering... I did this bridge' maps to opportunity for interesting work.
Quote about moving 'to business sector' is transferability, not variety of the field; does not support 'appealed because so varied'.
'engineering discipline can go to business sector as well' = good degree to have even outside the profession.
Problem-solving is valued but quote is about engineers' thinking style, not a draw-to-study; thin, keep low.
Father businessman, mother housewife; no family member in industry -> strongly disagree.
Mother warned it could be tough for a girl rather than encouraged; disagree defensible.
'My family, they are neutral' -> father did not encourage -> disagree.
Family not supportive/neutral; only a friend's mention sparked the idea, so 'nobody encouraged' is defensible.
Family neutral; no one discouraged studying engineering (father's discouragement was about placement).
'Yeah, I really like it' plus 'Very pleased that I'm in [this university]' supports strongly agree.
'find it quite interesting and the lecturers... willing to teach and patient' = satisfied with lectures.
Lecturers 'willing to teach and patient' -> satisfied with support from lecturers.
'my tutor he's been - done very well' -> satisfied with personal tutor support.
Friends were biggest positive influence; met a lot of new people -> satisfied with friends made.
'become a stronger person' is personal growth not clearly interpersonal skills from the course; thin, downgrade to low.
Fine with friends but annoyed by no-shows; mixed net stance -> neither satisfied nor dissatisfied.
Quote is about men being fair on mental work / helping with physical; says nothing about male vs female confidence in class.
Confirms intention to go on placement and gives reasons.
'I want some experiences in the civil industry' = primary work-experience reason; strongly agree defensible.
'get the job easier after I graduate' plus affirms it improves career prospects.
'I know what civil engineering is really like' = wants idea of what industry is really like.
'placement experience will help me make the decision' (consultant vs contractor).
Networking / knowing what to expect maps reasonably to personal development.
Quote is about LEARNING technical skills / learning more on site, not APPLYING theory learnt at university.
Rejects father's 'finish earlier' view -> does not want to finish uni ASAP -> disagree.
Concludes 'eventually I think I'll go into consulting' despite preferring contracting now.
'I'll carry on and an MSc programme' -> yes to further study.
Names an MSc -> Masters, MSc, MBA.
'Definitely being chartered' -> chartership important.
'senior engineer / responsible for quite large project' is ambiguous between managerial and technical; keep low.
Repeatedly cites wanting to travel; influences company choice -> travel important.
Quote notes salary not competitive but not its importance to her job choice; neutral is a thin default, keep low.
